title: Exhaustive Matching
story: You add a new variant to your enum — 'Pending' — and suddenly your code won't compile! The compiler found every match statement you forgot to update. This is exhaustive matching: the compiler as your safety net.
why: Exhaustive matching is XIOM's guarantee that you handle every possible case — the compiler rejects code with missing match arms, preventing runtime bugs at compile time.
analogy: Exhaustive matching is like a customs checklist — every passenger (value) must go through a lane (arm). If a new country opens (new variant), the checklist is updated before any plane lands.
try_it: Create an `enum Weather { Sunny, Rainy, Cloudy, Snowy }`. Write two functions that match on Weather: `needs_umbrella` and `needs_sunscreen`. Make sure both are exhaustive. Then add a new variant `Windy` — watch the compiler tell you exactly which functions need updating.
tips: The compiler is your friend — when it says 'non-exhaustive patterns,' it's preventing a future bug
Use `_` as the last arm for types with many possible values (integers, strings)
When you add a variant to an enum, let the compiler find all the match statements you need to update
common_mistakes: Adding a `_` catch-all early in the match — it eats all remaining cases, hiding missing specific patterns
Writing match arms after `_` — they'll never execute because `_` already matched everything
Assuming the compiler catches LOGIC errors — it only checks that all VARIANTS are covered, not that your logic is correct
